ai_show_review.summary: Fiery early‑70 set with epic China>Rider>High Time and soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert opens with a plaintive Black Peter before exploding into a high‑octane China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time sequence. Jerry’s guitar tone on High Time is called “perfect,” and Pigpen’s vocals soar on Good Lovin' and Turn On Your Lovelight. A tribal drum showdown propels the band through The Other One into an electrifying Lovelight climax.
ai_show_review.review: On March 7, 1970 at the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium the Dead delivered a blistering early‑70 performance that still feels fresh on today’s audience tapes. After a heartfelt Black Peter, the band launched into one of the era’s most ferocious medleys – China Cat Sunflower bleeding straight into I Know You Rider and then High Time – with Bob’s “burning” guitar work and Jerry’s flawless tone driving the momentum. Phil’s bass burst onto Good Lovin' like a machine‑gun, feeding a tribal Zulu‑tribe drum duel between Mickey and Billy that segued into The Other One’s frenetic soloing before soaring into Turn On Your Lovelight, where Pigpen’s vocal fire capped an unforgettable night. Despite the tape’s crackles and occasional pitch sharpness, the recording captures the band’s relentless energy and tight transitions, making it the definitive source for this legendary set.

best_recording.reason: Only available audience tape, but it preserves the epic China>Rider>High Time run and soaring Lovelight with decent instrument separation despite fair‑quality hiss and splices.

key_highlights: Epic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time medley that drives the set.
Tribal drum battle (Mickey & Billy) leading into a powerful Good Lovin' → The Other One sequence.
Soaring Turn On Your Lovelight climax highlighted by Pigpen’s vocal fire.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone on High Time is praised as perfect; his vocal on Black Peter is called emotional, and he delivers a fast, frenetic solo on The Other One.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass intro into Good Lovin' is described as a “machine‑gun” that punches through the wall between sections, providing a driving force throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s burning guitar work shines especially during the China > Rider transition; his rhythm playing is praised across the set.
band_performance.Pigpen: Pigpen’s vocal performance is lauded on Black Peter and Good Lovin', with his showmanship adding extra fire to the night.
band_performance.Mickey: The drum segment is depicted as tribal, “Zulu‑tribe” energy with powerful, stomping playing that fuels the band’s momentum.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann matches Mickey in delivering a tribal, high‑energy drum battle that propels the set into its climactic moments.
